Elliot rolled over, and the axe hit the ground where he had been standing a moment before.
He came up swinging, and his sword found the weak spot in the king’s armor, cutting a line of black blood across its ribs.
The monster screamed in pain and rage as it pulled its axe free and swung it in a wide arc.
Elliot ducked to avoid the blow, which made his hair fly up, and then he stabbed the king in the throat.
That attack should have worked.
Elliot’s form was flawless, the angle was ideal, and the opening was evident.
However, a small stone on the ground shifted at the last possible moment, rolling under Elliot’s boot and momentarily off-balance.
The thrust missed, making only a shallow cut on the king’s shoulder instead of going through the important area.
Rex smiled to himself from thirty yards away because it was his doing, with his hand slightly outstretched.
Telekinesis is a very useful tool when used carefully and manipulatively.
Elliot cursed under his breath and got back into position as the Goblin King took advantage of him.
"What the fuck... just happened...?"
The monster then attacked over and over; every swing of its huge axe was strong enough to break stone.
Elliot was excellent at parrying and dodging, and his sword work was a blur of defensive moves.
But Rex could see that things were getting worse.
Every blocked blow sent vibrations up Elliot’s arms, and every dodge had to be perfectly timed.
The hero was strong, even smart, but the Goblin King was so relentless that it would do anything to stop its enemies.
Elliot saw an opening and took it.
He pretended to go left, then turned right and drove his blade toward the king’s open flank.
The strike was perfectly aimed at the space between armor plates, where it would slide between ribs and stab vital organs.
Rex smirks, "I don’t think so..."
And then... a light breeze, not stronger than a breath, caught the blade in the middle of its thrust.
Not enough to be seen, but enough to change the angle by an inch.
The sword didn’t go deep, but instead, it scraped along the armor and made another shallow cut.
The Goblin King yelled and hit Elliot with its free hand, knocking him back across the chest and sending him flying.
He rolled with the blow and got up with a split lip and dented but still intact armor.
"W-What...?!
That’s impossible...!"
"Elliot!" Diana’s voice rang out, full of worry.
"I’m fine!" he yelled back, spitting blood and moving forward again.
"Get back!
I can handle this by myself!"
Rex, on the other hand, could see the truth.
Elliot was getting tired, and every attack that should have been the end of the fight somehow missed by the smallest of margins.
To everyone watching, it seemed like bad luck or the Goblin King’s unexpected speed.
Rex was the only one who knew the real reason.
The hero pushed himself forward with new strength, his sword trailing light as he used what was clearly a skill.
He screamed, "Heroic Strike!" and his sword glowed with golden energy.
The attack was powerful because it had speed, power, and skill that should have split the Goblin King in half.
Rex really thought about letting it land, which would have ended this joke early.
But nope!
This should have gone on longer for his research.
The heroes had to be pushed, tested, and made to show what they could really do.
As Elliot’s powerful sword came down toward the king’s head, Rex pushed a pebble near the monster’s foot with just a little bit of force.
The pebble shifted to the side, capturing the king’s attention for a fleeting moment, allowing it to shift its weight and raise its axe in a final attempt to block.
BAAMMM!!!
There was an explosion of sparks and magical energy when the weapons hit.
The impact knocked both fighters back, and Elliot’s attack spread out, but it left a deep cut in the Goblin King’s axe.
Elliot said, "No way... that’s impossible," in a shocked voice.
"That should have killed it with just one clear attack of my skill!"
The Goblin King also seemed surprised that he was still alive.
It looked at its broken weapon, then at Elliot, and its evil eyes seemed to show some respect.
The fight would not be an easy win for either of them, just because someone was intervening.
Helena watched with a shocked look that she didn’t expect to feel a magic that felt foreign near the Goblin King.
She reasoned that this goblin king was unique in that it possessed a form of magic that allowed it to defend itself against any threat.
"Oh my...
The world is becoming increasingly unusual... a goblin with protective magic is quite a novelty." Helena thought to herself while holding her cheek to observe their fight even further.
They went around each other, both breathing heavily and bleeding from many cuts.
The clearing had become eerily quiet, with everyone holding their breath as they watched the duel.
Then there was silence, and Diana’s voice broke it.
"Hey Elliot!
I’m not going to let you do this by yourself!"
"Diana, no!
Stay back!" Elliot yelled, but his sister was already on the move.

chapters.title: Chapter 40. Seems Like I Hit The Hero’s Ego (What a Naive Fool He Is)
paragraphs: An arrow flew by Elliot’s ear and hit the Goblin King in the shoulder dead on. The monster roared and turned to face this new threat, but another arrow hit it in the thigh.
Diana moved forward with her bow drawn, firing shots with perfect accuracy. Every arrow found a weak spot in the king’s armor and hit it, slowly breaking down his defenses.
Elliot yelled, "Diana, get out of here!" as he tried to get in between his sister and the monster.
"Nope! Not happening, brother! We fight it together as a family!" Diana shot three more arrows in quick succession, making the Goblin King raise its arm to protect itself.
Then a blast of light magic hit the monster’s chest, and Lily ran into the fight with her staff raised high. "I’m helping too!"
Elliot and Diana both yelled, "Lily, no!" at the same time.

But the youngest Starlight was already casting her spells, making magical shields that kept the Goblin King away from her siblings. The monster was hit by light bolts that burned its sickly green skin.
"What the fuck is she doing now...?" Rex looked at Lily with a conflicted look. "She’s going to ruin my perfect plan—"
GROOOOOAAAAGGGHHHHH!!!
The Goblin King roared in anger when he saw that he now had to fight three people instead of just one. It swung its axe in a big circle, making all three Starlights run away.
And then... Rex saw his chance and knew how to improve his next plan.
Diana had gone too far, but she was vulnerable because she was too focused on keeping the arrows flying. The Goblin King also saw it and turned to her with murder in its eyes.
The Goblin King raised its axe, preparing to strike.
"With this improved plan... I can probably get their respect for me even higher, and that’s fucking perfect!"
"Here goes nothing...!"
Rex stepped hard on the ground to gain momentum for running faster than ever before, aided by his telekinesis, which propelled him faster than his legs could move.
He got to Diana just as the axe was coming down, tackling her from the side and taking the brunt of a glancing blow to the shoulder.
The edge of the axe cut into Rex’s skin, and pain shot through his body. Not very deep, but deep enough to make him wince in pain. And then the blood on his cut quickly pooled, turning his shirt red.
"W-What...?! Rex!" Diana yelled as they fell to the ground in a tangle of arms and legs. "Why did you do that...!?"
"Stay down!" Rex grunted as he pushed himself up, even though it hurt. His shoulder hurt, but the wound was only superficial and looked worse than it was.
The Goblin King turned to face them and raised its axe to finish them off. Rex stood in front of Diana, ready to make it look like he was going to sacrifice himself.
"I would never do this shit again... that fucking hurt!" Rex thought to himself. "But with this opportunity... they’ll probably be more open to me and even trust me the most!"
Before the blow could land, Lily’s magic hit the monster’s face with a strong burst that made it stagger back.
"Don’t you DARE HURT HIIMMM!!!" Lily screamed, her voice shaking with anger.

Her magic radiated with an intensity Rex had never witnessed before, driven by genuine fear and anger. The Goblin King, seemingly unfazed by the attack, retaliated by striking Lily with the back of his hand, sending her hurtling through the air.
She landed hard and lay still for a moment.
"Lily!!!" Diana exclaimed, rising quickly from her spot. She was torn between rushing to her sister’s side and confronting the monster.
Rex made the choice for her. "Go to her! I’ll put it off!"
"But you’re injured...!"
"Forget about me! Just go save her!" Rex yelled back at her.
Diana hesitated for only a second before running to Lily’s side, cradling her sister, who was groaning but conscious.

Helena watched this scene unfold from across the battlefield with growing horror. This young man, who worked at the inn and seemed like a normal guy, had just put himself in danger to protect both of her daughters.
And what’s even more shocking is that he’s a reincarnator, and she had a lot of bad history about them being cocky and wanting to center everything around him like he’s some kind of a hero.
"This is a real sacrifice... coming from a reincarnator."
"My children... they’re being saved by someone not from this world." Helena thought to herself while both of her hands shook with horror.

Helena saw his shoulder was bleeding, and his face was pale with pain, but he still stood between the Goblin King and her girls. "Maybe I need to be more open to some of the reincarnators who are worthy of respect for their own cause..."
"Rex!" Helena shouted, her voice filled with motherly concern.
She started casting without thinking, and her magic was stronger and more focused than anything she had shown during training.
But before she could cast her spell, Elliot’s furious shout echoed through the clearing.
"Everyone...!!! STAAAND DOOOOWN!" He screamed so loud that it made Helena stop her spell mid-casting.
"This IS my FIGHT...!" The hero’s voice was full of anger and hurt pride. "I don’t need help from civilians or new people!"
"Get back! That’s an order from your hero!"
Diana quickly looked up. "Elliot, this Goblin King is too strong for only one person to handle!"
"I told you to fall back!" Elliot’s face was red with anger and shame.
His sisters and a random inn worker were stealing the show from the great hero Elliot Von Starlight, and it seems like Rex’s plan worked to start to show his true colors.
Rex thought to himself while hiding a smile behind his injured expression. "I fucking knew it... this wimp’s pride is easily hurt, and there’s no way he’s someone from this world with that attitude."
"But well... there’s some NPC that acted like that in every game or story, which is fun shit to see them fall down."
The more Rex undermined Elliot’s ego from the shadows, the more he understood the hero’s thoughts. Elliot wasn’t merely focused on protecting his family.
He was trying to prove something, that he could be the hero everyone thought he could be and win the glory all by himself.
And that kind of shit was perfect, just because Rex could deal with it all day long.
"I... am Elliot Von Starlight, and I’m here to save the world from any evil beings, including a goblin king like you!" Elliot starts to do his sword stance.
The Goblin King screamed, "UBASHAAAAAAA!!!"
Elliot charged the Goblin King again, this time with a sword that glowed with golden light. "HAAARRRGGGHHHH!!! I’LL FUCKING KILL YOU!!!"
He attacked more quickly now, fueled by pride and desperation. He was pushing himself too hard to get this over with quickly before anyone else could get in the way.
The Goblin King fought him back with an axe that sang through the air with deadly accuracy. They hit each other at a furious pace, neither giving up.
CLANG! CLANG! CLANG!
"Heh... keep trying harder, you naive fool." Rex said in a low tone.

chapters.title: Chapter 41. Something That I do For Her To Repay Me Soon! (Please Let it Be Her Body)
paragraphs: Rex, who was still close to Diana and Lily, used his telekinesis to expand his awareness. And it is time to show that Elliot isn’t the perfect hero this world needs.
When Elliot lunged forward with a thrust, Rex moved a small rock under his foot. The hero stumbled, his strike failed, and he found himself overextended.
Everyone was shocked seeing Elliot make a fool of himself just because he tripped on a small rock. "Oh no!"
The Goblin King’s axe came down in a brutal overhead chop that Elliot barely managed to block. And then... the blow knocked him to one knee.
"Elliot!" Diana cried out.

Elliot gritted his teeth and pushed back, struggling to stand despite the overwhelming strength of the monster pressing down on him. His arms trembled from the exertion, and beads of sweat trickled down his face.
Rex changed the way Elliot held his sword. He used a tiny amount of telekinesis to make his palm slide a little on the hilt.
"Just look at this fucking fool... he’s trying so hard."
Elliot’s counter swing lost power and hit the king’s armor instead of his flesh. "N-No...! Fuck...!!!"
"What the fuck is wrong with—"
The Goblin King struck Elliot with a headbutt, causing the hero’s face to collide with his thick skull. Elliot’s nose broke with a sickening crunch, and blood sprayed everywhere as he fell back.
"No, brother...!" Lily tried to get up, but Diana wouldn’t let her. "Let me go...! I want to help him!"
"No, Lily! Stay here! You’re not strong enough to face something like this!" the older sister yelled, even though she was scared for their brother and her face was pale.
Elliot tried to see better by wiping blood from his eyes. The Goblin King didn’t give him a chance; instead, he pushed forward with even more force.
Its axe came at him from all sides, and each swing got closer to killing him.
The hero was having trouble. His blocks were a little slower, and his dodges weren’t as clean. He would have been dead in a few more seconds.

Helena determined that she had witnessed enough. As she started casting a series of deadly spells, her hands wove intricate patterns. The air around her crackled with magic, and the power grew stronger and stronger.
"Flame Lance!" she shouted, and a spear of concentrated fire shot out of her hands and screamed toward the Goblin King.
The spell followed the monster even though it tried to get away. It hit its back and burned through its armor.
RAAAAAAAGGGHHHHHHH!!!
It roared in pain, which took its attention away from Elliot.
"Ice Shards!" Helena shouted again, not giving it a chance to catch its breath.
A flurry of sharp ice shards materialized and hurled forward, with each shard striking exposed skin and penetrating deeply.
Rex closely observes Helena’s magic and notes that she seems to be using basic spells that have been significantly enhanced.
This observation leads Rex to consider that in this world, magic can transform into anything, provided the user possesses enough energy and imagination to unleash it.
"Stone Fist!" The ground under the Goblin King exploded, and a huge structure of rock and dirt turned into a giant fist that punched up, hitting the monster in the chest and lifting it off its feet.
The king crashed back to the ground, injured and bleeding from multiple wounds. And for the first time, it appeared terrified as dark blood collected beneath it.
Helena moved forward, her magic building up for what was clearly going to be the final blow. "It’s time to end this madness!"
"Lightning... BOOLLTT!!!" she screamed, and it seemed like the sky answered her, with electricity gathering above her hand.
The Goblin King reacted unexpectedly upon realizing that it would die within seconds as Helena prepared her finishing blow.
RAAAAAAAAAGGGGHHHHH!!!
The king let out a desperate growl, and it must have used its skill, because its whole body suddenly filled with dark energy. Its wounds started to heal, and it felt stronger in its limbs.
Rex raised an eyebrow as he observed the Goblin King’s wound healing through regeneration, which briefly illuminated his thoughts. "Regeneration... That’s it...!"
Rex thought to himself. "I should’ve known earlier that regeneration is going to be such a fucking OP skill I can use for my manipulation..."

"With that... I could hurt myself without having to worry about dying, which means that I could trick everyone by trying to save them." Rex smirks. "I’ll add to my list soon... and debate which I should pick between foresight and infinite regeneration.
"RAAAAGGGGGHHHHHHH!!!" The Goblin King screamed even louder while punching his chest like a gorilla.
"What is it doing...?" Lily asked with a scared look.
"That’s his skill when he’s about to die... Berserk mode," Diana whispered in fear. "He’s entering a rage of death."

The Goblin King, who had been given power from the rage, raised his axe high and slammed it into the ground with all his might. The impact made a huge shockwave that spread out, ripping up the ground and sending a cloud of dust and debris flying across the battlefield.
It was nearly impossible for anyone to see clearly at that moment. The massive cloud of dust obscured their vision, transforming the clearing into a confusing, blind maze.
Helena’s lightning bolt went off into empty air because she couldn’t see her target anymore. "Tch!"
"Damn it!" she yelled, waving her hand to try to get rid of the dust.
"What a smart creature..." Her other hand held up a shield to protect her, knowing the king could attack from any side.

Rex closed his eyes, enabling his telekinetic awareness to precisely map his surroundings, even amidst the chaos. He could sense the location of everyone, including the Goblin King, tracking each of their movements.

The monster bent down and grabbed a huge boulder, at least the size of a horse cart, while the dust hid it. It was able to lift the huge stone and throw it right at where Helena stood, even though she couldn’t see it through the dust cloud.
Helena had no idea that death was approaching her quickly, and she was uncertain about how to defend herself.
That chance made Rex smirk with sinister knowledge, aware that this moment could bring him even closer to Helena in the future. It was something that had to be repaid after what he was about to do.
"HELENAAAA!!!" Rex shouted, filled with determination, trying to sound like a hero ready to sacrifice himself.
He ran through the dust, his telekinesis guiding him straight to Helena’s location. She came out of the fog just as he got there, and her eyes went wide when she saw him running toward her.
"Rex? What are you—"

She came out of the fog just as he got there, and her eyes went wide when she saw him running toward her.
"Rex?
What are you—"

chapters.title: Chapter 42. It was All Worth The Trust (It’s Time To Break Them One by One)
paragraphs: He slammed into her, wrapped his arms around her waist, and used his telekinesis to push them both to the side. At the same time, he pushed on the boulder that was flying toward them.
It didn’t stop, but it did slow down just a little bit.
The timing was just right. The boulder, which was going slower because of Rex’s secret help, still hit both of them as they dove.
Instead of turning them into paste, it pushed them back with a lot of force, sending them across the ground until they hit a tree.
Rex put his body between Helena and the tree, taking the hit on his already hurt shoulder and back. Pain shot through him, real this time, as the bark broke and his breath left his lungs.

"Fucking hell...! I went all through this just to get their pussy as the payback... what a fucking joke." Rex thought to himself. "But I fucking knew it was going to be worth it... especially after I held Helena like this... she smells so fucking good!"
They fell to the ground in a pile, with Helena lying on Rex’s chest and Rex on his back. The boulder came to a stop a few feet away, having lost its deadly speed.
Helena pushed herself up slightly, placed her hands on Rex’s chest, and gazed down at him in disbelief. "Y... Y-You saved me..."
"You knew it was going to happen, and... you still saved me... even with that condition of yours."
"Yeah... I see its silhouette grabbing the boulder that’s trying to hit you..." Rex managed to gasp, wincing as the pain intensified. "But forget about that... are you okay?"
"I’m fine, but you..." She looked at his shoulder, where fresh blood was seeping through his shirt, and at how he winced when he tried to move. "You’ve been hurt badly..."
"Do you know how to stop yourself from saving someone...? You’ve done enough by saving my daughter... you don’t have to do this to an old hag like me," Helena said with an embarrassed look.
"Don’t talk like that, Helena... you’re no old hag," Rex said with a weak smile. "I’ll make sure to live as long as I can keep going to save someone I care about."
"And of course one of them is to keep you safe, and it’s worth it." Rex showed his charming smile that shot through her heart right away.
Helena’s eyes changed. She looked at this young man who had put himself in danger twice to protect her daughters and now her.

All of this was done without hesitation, even though they were hurt. Rex couldn’t check the system while still pretending to be hurt, but her desire level was definitely going up after he saved her and then said something charming like that.
The dust was beginning to clear, revealing the rest of the battlefield. Elliot had used the confusion to recover, his face set with grim determination despite his broken nose and multiple cuts.
He screamed, "THIS...ENDS! NOOOOOW!!!" and put all of his strength into his sword.
The blade shone with a bright golden light, brighter than before, and power throbbed along its edge. "Ultimate Heroic Strike!"
Elliot flew at the Goblin King like a meteor, his powerful sword aimed right at the monster’s heart. This was his strongest attack, the result of all his training and heroic strength.
It would definitely kill the King of the Goblins.
Unless... Rex got in the way one last time.
As Elliot got closer, Rex used a tiny bit of telekinesis on the hero’s leading foot. He used just enough telekinesis to cause the hero to stumble again, altering his path by a few inches.
Elliot’s last attack didn’t go through the Goblin King’s heart. Instead, it cut across its chest and shoulder. A terrible wound, yes, but not one that would kill him right away.
The hero’s speed took him past the monster, and he fell to the ground, out of energy and out of attacks.
The Goblin King, wounded and furious, recognized his opportunity. It lifted its huge axe to kill Elliot and get ready to split his skull.
In a split second, Rex made up his mind to end his perfect plan so that in the upcoming future, he doesn’t need to act like something he hated because all of it was done for today.
"Let’s fucking do it... I’m going to get hurt for the last time just to protect that fucking wimp so that by this chance... his girlfriend is going to slowly lower his guard for me." Rex smirks.

He pushed himself up from where he was lying next to Helena, ignoring her protests and the pain in his body. Using his telekinesis, he moved faster than any human should be able to, rapidly narrowing the distance between him and Elliot.
Everyone who saw Rex run at an impossible speed saw him get behind the fallen hero just as the Goblin King’s axe came down.
"This is... the greatest plan of a fucking mastermind." Rex starts to laugh out loud inside his mind that he had done it.
The axe hit Rex hard across the back, knocking him forward and to his knees. The wound bled hot, red blood that stained the ground below him.
SLASSHHH!
"REX!!!" several voices screamed at the same time. Lily, Diana, Helena, and even some of the villagers.
Rex fell forward on his hands and knees, with blood pouring from the cut on his back. The pain was real, and so was the wound, but he had used his telekinesis to make it look worse than it was.
"This pain... I’ve already grown accustomed to it from my past life, where I endured many cuts and bruises."
"However, with my telekinesis, I can at least ensure the wounds don’t appear critical." Rex thought to himself, gritting his teeth to stifle any sounds of pain, unwilling to show weakness.

He could feel the blood loss starting to have an effect on him, and he could see his vision starting to narrow. He carefully used his telekinesis to put pressure on the wound from the inside, pinching off blood vessels that had been cut and stopping fatal bleeding.
He did this while everyone else stood in shock, and naturally, in such a chaotic situation, no one would question how he managed to do all of that to save everyone he could.
Anyone who saw him would have thought he was dead after taking a blow that should have killed him to save Elliot’s life.
The Goblin King raised its axe again, this time to kill both of them. Elliot couldn’t move because he was too tired, and Rex couldn’t move because he was hurt.
This was it... Rex was gambling to see what would happen next after he had done everything he could to make them all fully trust him.
And then... Evelyn stepped up with a determination in her eyes. "That’s enough..."
She moved like lightning, and suddenly she had her sword in her hand, even though no one had seen her draw it. Her eyes radiated a power beyond this world, undoubtedly amplified by the system.
At that moment, Rex saw it. Evelyn had been concealing her true skills by playing a supportive role while Elliot received all the credit.
But the sight of her boyfriend almost dying and Rex sacrificing his life to save him shattered any control she had over herself.
"I’ll finish this right now," Evelyn said in a cold, firm voice.
Her blade moved in a way that was too quick to follow, leaving a trail of light behind it. In the brief moment between heartbeats, she positioned herself behind the Goblin King.
"Holy shit... she’s fast..." Rex was shocked seeing she had an OP skill.
There was a moment of perfect stillness.
Then the Goblin King’s head came off its shoulders and hit the ground with a wet thump. Its huge body swayed for a moment before falling to the ground, really dead this time.
Evelyn stood over the dead body with a clean blade, her face carefully blank. But when her eyes found Rex lying on the ground, bleeding and unconscious, they held something complicated.
It was gratitude, and even higher than that, it was respect. Perhaps this marked the beginning of her trust in him, as he had just proven his worth.
And now... just because of that, Evelyn had shown them how powerful she was. Rex’s rescue of Elliot unveiled a secret she had evidently been hiding.
Rex didn’t expect that at all, but it’s still part of the plan and perfect in every way.
"Heh... I’ve won..." Rex smirks.

Rex let his arms go limp and fell all the way to the ground. His telekinesis kept the pressure on the wound, which kept him from really dying, but to everyone else, it looked like he was getting weaker and weaker.
"Rex, no...! Stay with me!" Lily said, her hands glowing with healing magic and tears streaming down her face.
"Oi! Don’t you dare die like that...!" Diana said, putting her hands on her sister’s to help with the healing.
Helena pushed through, and her stronger magic was already casting healing spells. "That’s enough, girls! Let your mother handle this!"
Rex felt satisfied seeing Lily, Diana, and even Helena tried to help him. He knew their desire had likely increased, and all he had to do was execute it more until he could get them all at once.
Elliot crawled over, his face pale with shock and shame. "Why... why would you save me, Rex...?"
"I’ve failed as a hero... just because I let someone save me!"
Rex smiled weakly, even though his lips were bleeding. "Because... heroes shouldn’t die... in a dumb way..."
"But all of that bullshit was a lie... of course..." Rex thought to himself.
Then he slowly closed his eyes and trusted his telekinesis to keep him alive while everyone else freaked out.
"Shit... I can’t keep my eyes open... I’m fucking exhausted..."
"Oh well... when I wake up... it’s time to make another plan..."
He had gotten hurt in ways that would have killed a normal person. He had saved three Starlights, one of whom was the hero himself.
He made Evelyn show her hidden power because he was grateful and respected her. And all of this would make him seem like a trustworthy, heroic person who was worth protecting and trusting.
The manipulation had gone perfectly.
Now he just had to get through the aftermath and enjoy the benefits...

chapters.title: Chapter 43. The Most Profitable Near-Death Experience in History
paragraphs: The first thing Rex noticed as he slowly woke up was... PAIN.
It wasn’t the sharp, immediate pain he felt when the Goblin King’s axe hit him, but it was more like a dull, all-over ache that seemed to come from every part of his body.

His shoulder hurt where he had taken the first hit to protect Diana, his back felt like it had been ripped apart and poorly put back together, and even doing the most human thing, like breathing, hurt his ribs.
"Grrgghhh... fucking hell," Rex thought as he woke up. "Remember... even when you change the damage, getting hit with big axes still hurts so fucking bad."

"It better be worth it in the future because I’ll fucking remember this moment for the rest of my life..." Rex tried to open his eyes, but they were heavy and didn’t want to work with him. "Ah yeah... I almost fucked up."

"Lily... Diana... Helena... Evelyn... better prepare yourself because the pain in my body will only be healed fully with all of your bodies." Rex already holds the grudge when the pain keeps getting to him.

After a few tries, his eyelids finally opened, showing him a ceiling that he didn’t recognize right away. He saw wooden beams, a simple building, and a single lantern hanging from a hook, emitting a warm, flickering light.
Rex realized that he was in a room at the inn, and it seemed like someone carried him all the way here. "Huh... at least I’m back here at my checkpoint."
Rex slowly turned his head, wincing because his neck muscles were hurting, and stopped when he saw Lily.
Lily was fast asleep on the floor next to his bed, her head resting on the mattress near his hand. Rex noticed the lines of dried tears on her cheeks, but her face appeared calm in slumber.
Her hand was outstretched toward him, and her fingers barely touched his arm, as if she had fallen asleep while holding onto him.
"Well," Rex thought, "what an adorable girl... I can’t believe she’s going to stay there, waiting for me to wake up."
"She’s really a good girl after all... I’ll reward her properly soon." Rex smirks when he is about to do something to her.
But then... the door opened quietly, and Mara came in with a basin of water and clean rags. When she saw Rex’s open eyes, she froze.
"A-Ahh...!" Her own eyes went wide with shock and relief.
"R-Rex," she said, breathing heavily as she put the basin down so quickly that water spilled over the sides. "You’re... awake!"
Mara showed a genuine smiles after knowing that Rex was alive and well, "Thank Goodness...! You’re awake!"

She crossed the room in three quick steps and threw her arms around him, burying her face in his neck before he could say anything. He could feel wetness on his skin and her whole body shaking, which told him she was crying.
Mara whispered fiercely, "I thought I’d lost you..."
She wrapped her arms around him tightly, even though he was hurt. "When they brought you back... there was so much blood!"
"You wouldn’t wake up, and I... I thought..."
Knowing Mara acted like that made Rex can’t hide his smile at all, "You’d think I’ll just die like that...? Oh please, don’t make me laugh."

Rex put his good arm around her, even though it hurt, and he thinks this was a big deal. This was Mara being completely open with her feelings, showing her full devotion and attachment that couldn’t be faked.
The innkeeper, once cold and distant, had vanished from his presence. There was a woman there who had been scared of losing someone she really needed.
Rex said softly, "Alright, alright, I’m okay now," and he ran his hand through her hair. "But... it still hurts like hell, even though I’m totally fine."
"A giant goblin can’t kill me, like I said."
Mara pulled back just enough to see his face; her hands were on his cheeks. "Don’t ever do something that dumb again, do you hear me?!
"Don’t you dare put yourself in a dangerous situation like that without any experience of fighting a monster!"
"Nope. I saved people, including the hero and his family. That’s not dumb." Rex loathed himself for saying that, but he still wanted to earn Mara’s trust.
"It’s dumb when you almost die doing it," Mara said, her voice full of emotion. "I don’t care about heroes or their families!"
"I only care about you!"

It was everything Rex had worked for to hear her say that. Rex could hear the possessiveness in her voice, the raw need. Mara was completely his, devoted to him beyond reason, and willing to put him above everything else, even her own husband.
Rex laughed inside his mind. "HAHAHA! I can’t fucking believe she just said that... she really wants me only, huh?"
"Alright," Rex said, bringing her close again. "I know, and I’m sorry I scared you, but I’m here now, and I’m not going anywhere."
"C’mere..." Rex brings her face closed just to kiss her lips, and Mara closes both her eyes to enjoy it.

They stayed like that for what felt like an eternity, with Mara clinging to him as if she feared he would vanish if she let go. With each passing moment, the kiss grew increasingly passionate, and Mara, as always, couldn’t help but let out soft moans.
Finally, after being satisfied with the erotic kiss, she pulled away and wiped her eyes.
"You need to eat something after waking up from that," she said, her instincts as an innkeeper coming back. "Helena said your injuries were bad, but you’d get better with rest and good care."
"I made porridge for you, which is easy on your stomach."
"Phew~! That sounds great. Go get it for me, Mara." Rex ordered.
"Okay, wait for a sec." Mara nodded and turned to get the porridge she had brought.
"Time to check on something first..." Rex pulled up his system interface with a thought.
[RECOVERY STATUS]
[INJURIES: MODERATE, HEALING NORMALLY]
[TELEKINETIC PRESSURE MAINTAINING WOUND STABILITY]
[ESTIMATED FULL RECOVERY: 3-4 DAYS WITH REST]
Perfect, like he wanted, where his gambit had worked perfectly. The injuries looked severe but weren’t actually life-threatening thanks to his careful control during the attack.

"Tonight I really need to grind more desire energy, and it seems like I could pull up with something soon." Rex held his chin. "Foresight and Infinite Regeneration sounds good enough for me to be the strongest."
But more importantly...
[DESIRE LEVEL UPDATES]
[HELENA VON STARLIGHT: 40/100]
[INCREASE: +18 POINTS]
[STATUS: DEEPLY GRATEFUL, MATERNAL AFFECTION DEVELOPING]
"Maternal affection...? Holy fucking shit, now that... was a good one that I can’t wait to enjoy it myself!"
[DIANA VON STARLIGHT: 20/100]
[INCREASE: +12 POINTS]
[STATUS: RESPECT ESTABLISHED, ATTRACTION BEGINNING]
"She’s going to be next after I’m done with Lily..."
[LILY VON STARLIGHT: 90/100]
[INCREASE: +5 POINTS]
[STATUS: DEVOTION NEAR MAXIMUM, EMOTIONAL DEPENDENCY COMPLETE]
"I can see that..."
[EVELYN ASTRALIGHT: 15/100]
[INCREASE: +9 POINTS]
[STATUS: TRUST ESTABLISHED, GRATITUDE SIGNIFICANT]
Rex had to hold back a smile and laugh. The Goblin King incident had been worth every bit of pain.
In just one afternoon, Helena’s score went from 22 to 40 percent. Diana’s score had more than doubled from where she started.
Evelyn, who was the hardest person to get to know, had finally started to respect him, allowing him to approach her without worrying about raising any suspicion.
And Lily... she was at 90% desire, and she only needed ten more points to reach her maximum, which would make her another devoted energy source for his desire manifestation system.
"Just fucking wait, Elliot... I’ll make sure all your family members are mine." When Rex was just about to laugh like a maniac, but then...
"Here," Mara said, coming back with a bowl of hot porridge.
She sat on the edge of the bed and took a spoonful. "Let me help you."
Rex said, "I can feed myself," in a mild protest.
"I know you can, but... let me do this anyway." Her eyes begged him for help, not because of his injuries, but because she needed to take care of him and feel useful.
"Heh... this woman..."

There was a woman there who had been scared of losing someone she really needed.
Rex said softly, "Alright, alright, I’m okay now," and he ran his hand through her hair.
"But... it still hurts like hell, even though I’m totally fine."
"A giant goblin can’t kill me, like I said."
Mara pulled back just enough to see his face; her hands were on his cheeks.
"Don’t ever do something that dumb again, do you hear me?!
"Don’t you dare put yourself in a dangerous situation like that without any experience of fighting a monster!"
"Nope.
I saved people, including the hero and his family.
That’s not dumb." Rex loathed himself for saying that, but he still wanted to earn Mara’s trust.
"It’s dumb when you almost die doing it," Mara said, her voice full of emotion.
"I don’t care about heroes or their families!"
"I only care about you!"
It was everything Rex had worked for to hear her say that.
Rex could hear the possessiveness in her voice, the raw need.
Mara was completely his, devoted to him beyond reason, and willing to put him above everything else, even her own husband.
Rex laughed inside his mind.
"HAHAHA!
I can’t fucking believe she just said that... she really wants me only, huh?"
"Alright," Rex said, bringing her close again.
"I know, and I’m sorry I scared you, but I’m here now, and I’m not going anywhere."
"C’mere..." Rex brings her face closed just to kiss her lips, and Mara closes both her eyes to enjoy it.
They stayed like that for what felt like an eternity, with Mara clinging to him as if she feared he would vanish if she let go.
With each passing moment, the kiss grew increasingly passionate, and Mara, as always, couldn’t help but let out soft moans.
Finally, after being satisfied with the erotic kiss, she pulled away and wiped her eyes.
"You need to eat something after waking up from that," she said, her instincts as an innkeeper coming back.
"Helena said your injuries were bad, but you’d get better with rest and good care."
"I made porridge for you, which is easy on your stomach."
"Phew~!
That sounds great.
Go get it for me, Mara." Rex ordered.
"Okay, wait for a sec." Mara nodded and turned to get the porridge she had brought.
"Time to check on something first..." Rex pulled up his system interface with a thought.
[RECOVERY STATUS]
[INJURIES: MODERATE, HEALING NORMALLY]
[TELEKINETIC PRESSURE MAINTAINING WOUND STABILITY]
[ESTIMATED FULL RECOVERY: 3-4 DAYS WITH REST]
Perfect, like he wanted, where his gambit had worked perfectly.
The injuries looked severe but weren’t actually life-threatening thanks to his careful control during the attack.
"Tonight I really need to grind more desire energy, and it seems like I could pull up with something soon." Rex held his chin.
"Foresight and Infinite Regeneration sounds good enough for me to be the strongest."
But more importantly...
[DESIRE LEVEL UPDATES]
[HELENA VON STARLIGHT: 40/100]
[INCREASE: +18 POINTS]
[STATUS: DEEPLY GRATEFUL, MATERNAL AFFECTION DEVELOPING]
"Maternal affection...?
Holy fucking shit, now that... was a good one that I can’t wait to enjoy it myself!"
[DIANA VON STARLIGHT: 20/100]
[INCREASE: +12 POINTS]
[STATUS: RESPECT ESTABLISHED, ATTRACTION BEGINNING]
"She’s going to be next after I’m done with Lily..."
[LILY VON STARLIGHT: 90/100]
[INCREASE: +5 POINTS]
[STATUS: DEVOTION NEAR MAXIMUM, EMOTIONAL DEPENDENCY COMPLETE]
"I can see that..."
[EVELYN ASTRALIGHT: 15/100]
[INCREASE: +9 POINTS]
[STATUS: TRUST ESTABLISHED, GRATITUDE SIGNIFICANT]
Rex had to hold back a smile and laugh.
The Goblin King incident had been worth every bit of pain.
In just one afternoon, Helena’s score went from 22 to 40 percent.
Diana’s score had more than doubled from where she started.
Evelyn, who was the hardest person to get to know, had finally started to respect him, allowing him to approach her without worrying about raising any suspicion.
And Lily... she was at 90% desire, and she only needed ten more points to reach her maximum, which would make her another devoted energy source for his desire manifestation system.
"Just fucking wait, Elliot...
I’ll make sure all your family members are mine." When Rex was just about to laugh like a maniac, but then...
"Here," Mara said, coming back with a bowl of hot porridge.
She sat on the edge of the bed and took a spoonful.
"Let me help you."
Rex said, "I can feed myself," in a mild protest.
"I know you can, but... let me do this anyway." Her eyes begged him for help, not because of his injuries, but because she needed to take care of him and feel useful.
"Heh... this woman..."

chapters.title: Chapter 44. The Most Productive Bedridden Morning in History
paragraphs: Rex gave in and let her feed him like he was a baby. It was humiliating in a way, but it also felt excellent.
This was Mara giving in completely to her desire to serve him, be close to him, and have any reason to be close to him.

They were halfway through the bowl when Lily moved and lifted her head from where it had been resting on the bed. She slowly opened her eyes, which were unfocused and confused for a moment before they fell on Rex.
Then they got very big.
"Mm... Rex...?" She mumbled softly.
Then, shouting loud, "REX...!"
In her hurry, she almost knocked over the chair next to the bed as she got up from the floor. She was already crying before she even got to him.
"You’re awake...! You’re REALLY awake, Rex...!"
"I was so scared... I thought you were going to die!"
"There was so much blood, and you wouldn’t wake up, and nobody could tell me if you’d be okay...!"
"I’ve been sitting here for hours just waiting and hoping while praying that you’d open your eyes and..."
"Hwaahhhhhhhh! Rex!" She threw herself at him, wrapping her arms around his neck and crying into his shoulder as the words came out in a jumbled rush.
Mara quickly moved the bowl of porridge to the side so that Lily could get to it. "My... my... she’s really worried about you, Rex..."
"Shh," Rex said, putting his good arm around her to calm her down. "Don’t worry, Lily..."
"I’m right here," Rex said while hiding his smirk and thought to himself. "It’s already over for this girl... seems like she’s going to be all over me like Mara."
Lily cried, "You almost died... for my brother... and for all of us...!"
"It would have been my fault because I pushed you to help when I should have stayed back...!"
"If you had died, I don’t know what I would have done because I can’t lose you, Rex... I just... can’t..."
"Hey, shh, look at me," Rex said softly, tilting her head up with his hand. "I’m not going anywhere..."
"I’m too stubborn to let something like that kill me."
Lily’s eyes were red and swollen from crying, and they met his with a desperate look. "Promise me you won’t do that again!"
"Promise me you’ll be more careful the next time you try to help someone!"
"I promise I’ll try to be more careful," Rex said, which was as close to a lie as he could get without her noticing. "But I promise I will protect the people I care about if they are in danger."
Then he thought to himself. "I want to puke after saying that shit..."
Lily said again, "The people you... care about," in a small voice.
"Do you... do you care about me, Rex?"
This was it... This was the moment he had been eagerly anticipating.
Lily was completely open, emotionally raw, and in need of love and validation. He just had to give her what she wanted.
Rex said softly, "Of course I care about you, Lily."
"You’re smart, kind, and brave. Why wouldn’t I care about you?" Rex’s face looked charming right away for Lily’s eyes.
It was enough to make tears fall from her eyes again, but these were different. Not tears of fear, but tears of strong emotion.
"I... love you," Lily said, and the words came out of her like a dam that had finally broken. "I know I shouldn’t..."
"I know it’s probably wrong or inappropriate or too soon... but I can’t help it anymore!"
"I’ve never felt like this about anyone... You make me feel seen and valued and special in ways nobody else ever has!"
"You listen to me and treat me like an adult, and you’re kind and brave, and when I thought you might die... I realized I couldn’t imagine my life without you in it, and..."
"I love you, Rex! I love you so much that it hurts...!"
She was crying more now, as if the confession had broken something inside her. "I know you probably don’t feel the same way..."
"I’m twenty years old... and inexperienced, and there are better women out there for you, but... I needed you to know..."
"I needed to tell you before something else happened and I lost my chance. I just..."
"Lily," Rex said softly, cutting her off. "Take a breath for me..."
She gasped and took a shuddering breath, and her whole body shook in his arms.
Rex said, "I care about you too," which was true in his own messed-up way.
He cared about her like someone cares about a prized possession. "More than you might think."
"Re... Really?" Lily’s voice was so hopeful that it hurt.
"Really... you’re special, Lily." Rex smiled. "Don’t let anyone make you think differently."
She put her face back in his chest, but this time her tears seemed to be less heavy. Not desperation, but relief.
She held on to him like he was the only thing that was real in a world that was always changing. Rex held her close, feeling her desire rise to those last few important points.
[LILY VON STARLIGHT: 93/100]
[STATUS: LOVE CONFESSION MADE]
[EMOTIONAL VULNERABILITY: MAXIMUM]
[PROJECTED MAXIMUM THRESHOLD: 24-48 HOURS]
Only seven more points. And with Lily in this state, completely open and devoted, those points would be easy to get.

"My, my, you really are an adorable girl, Lily." Mara, who had been watching this scene with surprising calm, lightly touched Lily’s shoulder. "Now that you’ve already confessed... let him eat, dear."
"He needs to get more strength and energy to recover fast."
Lily reluctantly pulled away and wiped her eyes. "O-Oh! I’m sorry, I didn’t mean to... I just..."
Rex told her, "It’s okay."
"Your concern means a lot to me."
Mara started feeding him porridge again, and Lily sat down on the edge of the bed and held his hand tightly. They were quiet and almost like a family for a few minutes.
After that, someone knocked on the door.
Rex said, "Come in.
Helena walked in, looking elegant even though she was clearly tired. She looked straight at Rex, and when she saw him awake and eating, she looked relieved.
"Rex, thank goodness..." she said in a warm voice. "It’s good to see you well awake."
"How are you feeling currently?"
Rex said with a wry smile, "Like I got hit by a giant axe, but ehh... still alive and well."
Helena chuckled softly. "I guess that’s right."
She looked at Lily and Mara. "Can you both give us a minute?"
"I need to talk to Rex about some things in private."
Lily didn’t want to leave, but Mara got up right away. "Of course, Lady Helena."
Mara held Lily’s shoulder to bring her. "Let’s go, Lily... Let’s leave them alone."
"Okay..." Lily nodded, and then she and Mara left the room immediately.
Helena pulled the chair closer to the bed and sat down after the two women left. Her face was serious, but it was also warm.
"I wanted to say thank you," she said. "For saving my daughters and for saving all of us, really."
"What you did out there was incredibly brave."
Rex said, "I just did what needed to be done."
"No," Helena said, shaking her head. "You did a lot more than that."
"You put yourself in danger for my family several times, almost died in the process, and didn’t ask for anything in return."
"That kind of selflessness is rare, especially from..."
She stopped for a moment, as if she were carefully choosing her words.
"Especially from reincarnators?" Rex finished for her.
"Yes..." Helena nodded and then asked. "Do you know that Evelyn is the same as you...?"
"Yeah, she’s a reincarnator like me, I figured it out during the fight because of her skills that were too sharp and too practiced."
"She must have been granted an incredible power in this second life to move that fast."
Helena said, "She confronted me after the fight."
"She told me everything... starting from her system, her powers, and why she’s been hiding them."
"She was worried that everyone might have noticed and wanted to make sure her secret was safe, especially for you too."
Rex promised her, "Of course I won’t tell anyone... why would I do that?"
"That’s what I wanted to talk about," Helena said. "Evelyn doesn’t know that you’re also a reincarnator."
"She said she couldn’t scan you properly, which made her suspicious, but she hasn’t figured it out yet."
Rex’s brain worked fast. "Do you want me to keep it that way?"
Helena said, "I’m asking if you’d rather it that way."
"I won’t tell anyone your secret without your permission, but I wanted you to know that I know and give you a choice about what to do next."

chapters.title: Chapter 45. The Savior They Deserved, The Villain They Got
paragraphs: Rex found this intriguing. Helena was giving him control over information, showing trust and deference.
It was a power play, whether she realized it or not, putting him in her debt while simultaneously offering him something valuable.
After a moment, Rex said, "I’d rather not talk about it right now."
"Some people have certain expectations and biases about reincarnators. I’d rather be judged on what I do than where I came from."
"That makes sense," Helena said. "Alright then... I’ll keep your secret."
"Consider it a small repayment for saving my family."
"That’s not necessary," Rex protested. "I didn’t save them expecting payment."
"I know," Helena said in a soft voice. "That’s why I want to repay you."
"Rex, you’ve earned the gratitude of House Starlight, and that’s not something given lightly. If there’s anything you need, anything at all, you can ask it to me, okay?"
The offer hovered between them, brimming with potential. Rex could almost see the doors opening and the chances coming up.
Rex thought to himself. "She just said that to me... what a fucking stupid bitch, even if I ask her to suck my cock... seems like it’s not a good time for it."
He said, "I’ll think about it."
"Right now, I’m just trying to get better."
Helena smiled and had a knowing look in her eyes. "Of course... but if you don’t mind, I’d like to offer you something right away."
Rex was shocked hearing that, but then he tried to look excited rather than calm. "Huh...? What kind of offer?"

"When you’re feeling better, I’d like to give you a real healing massage," Helena said while clasping both her hands. "Not just the usual medical treatment, but something to help with the deeper tissue damage and to speed up the healing process."
"I know some restorative touch techniques that go beyond simple magic."
The way she said it and the slight blush on her cheeks made it seem like this was more personal than a normal medical procedure. Rex’s system helpfully gave background information.
[HELENA VON STARLIGHT: DESIRE 40/100 → 43/100]
[OBSERVATION: SUBJECT SEEKING PHYSICAL CONTACT]
[OBSERVATION: OFFER CONTAINS SUBTLE ROMANTIC UNDERTONES]

"She’s pushing it now, huh...? Seems like Helena can be my next target after I’m done with Lily," Rex thought to himself. "Imagine doing a threesome with the mother and the daughter... good shit right there."
"That sounds great... even though I don’t want to bother you more," Rex said. "But... thanks, Helena."
"Oh, come on now... don’t say that. I insist." She stood up and smoothed out her dress. "Alright, for now... get some good rest, Rex."
"Me and my family owe everything to what you’ve done for today."
When she turned to leave, she stopped at the door and looked back at him with a small smile and a wink that was definitely not motherly.
After that, she was gone, and Rex was left alone with his thoughts and his growing desire.
Rex smirked. "Oh my fucking lust... I can’t believe it, that’s a good signal for me to seduce her! I can’t believe MILFs are so fucking easy to be teased with."
Over the next hour, he received a parade of visitors.
Diana came first, looking uncomfortable but determined. She thanked him stiffly for saving her life.
Her professional demeanor couldn’t completely hide the warmth that was really there. She stayed for ten minutes, and as they talked about archery and strategy, she started to feel more relaxed.
By the time she left, her desire level had gone up another point.
[DIANA VON STARLIGHT: DESIRE 20/100 → 25/100]
Evelyn came with Elliot. The woman with the dark purple hair was usually very cautious, but this time she was genuinely thankful.
"I was wrong about you," she said simply. "I was suspicious when I should have been welcoming..."
"You saved Elliot’s life when I couldn’t get to him in time, and with that... I’ll never be able to repay you enough after everything you’ve done for us."
Rex said, "You don’t owe me anything."
"I’m just happy that he’s okay."
Elliot, looking humble and still wearing bandages from his own injuries, held Rex’s hand tightly. "You saved my life when you should have been saving yourself..."
"You took a blow meant for me, and... I don’t know how to thank you for that."
Rex smiled sarcastically and said, "Maybe next time you shouldn’t rush into fights alone."
"Let your family help you."
Elliot’s face showed that he had learned something from this. "Yeah... I will! And that’s a promise!"
"Rex, if you ever need anything from me, just ask for it, okay? I mean it because you’ve saved my life."
"I will. (just give me your fucking girlfriend so that I can break her and make her mine)." Rex had to use a lot of positive expression even though behind that face... he was disgusted.
And after a small talk with Elliot and Evelyn. Rex was alone again after they left.
He looked up at the ceiling and thought about everything that had happened.
His plan had been executed flawlessly. Almost too perfectly.
Everyone in the Starlight family now considered him to be a hero, a savior, and a person they could trust. Helena had jumped to 43 percent and was offering intimate massage sessions.
Diana was getting more and more interested in him. Lily was at 93 percent and had really confessed to him that she loved him.
But... Evelyn, the hardest target, was at 15 percent and still in the process of going up, and Rex knew that she was going to be a hard one because she’s a reincarnator.

And in the next two days, the bandits would strike just like he planned. Another chance to make himself look like a hero and protector, to strengthen the bonds he made during the crisis, and to pull everyone even deeper into his web.
Rex began to laugh. "Heh... hehehe..."
At first, he was quiet, but then he started to laugh harder and harder until he was shaking with real joy, even though it hurt his injuries.
"HAHAHAHAHAHA!!!"
"This is too fucking easy," he said between laughs. "They’re all so desperate for a savior that they’ll take anyone who can play the part well enough."
"Even though it makes me want to puke every time I do that, soon... when I’m strong enough, then I can take anything with force!" Rex said while clenching both his fists.
He sobered after a moment, his mind already racing ahead to next steps. Lily needed ten more points to reach her highest score.
Helena was making positive progress and might soon be ready for more direct manipulation. Diana was coming along. Even Evelyn was finally starting to trust him.
And Mara... she was all his, body and soul, and every time they have sex, she gives him desire energy to get every power he wants.
Speaking of which...
The afternoon turned into evening. Some villagers came by to thank him, and the Starlight family checked on him several times.
Over time, the stream of visitors slowed down and then stopped.
Rex was alone with his thoughts and plans again by the time night fell.
As the inn got ready for the night, he heard movement downstairs. Garrett’s voice rose as he told Mara that he was going fishing again tonight.
It seems that there was a rare night fish that only came out during certain phases of the moon, and tonight was perfect for it.
"I’ll be gone until morning," Garrett said. "Are you going to be okay?"
"Of course," Mara said, and her voice was normal. "Rex is recovering from his injuries, and I’ll monitor the situation closely."
Garrett exclaimed, "I’ve always known that Rex is a good man from the beginning! I’m a day one fan indeed, hahaha."
"He’s a real hero, and we’re lucky to have him as our worker." Garrett smiles.
Rex thought with dark amusement, "If only he knew."
He heard Garrett leave and the inn lock up for the night. Then there were footsteps on the stairs.
Mara quietly walked into his room and shut the door behind her. The light from the lamp made her look beautiful and a little messy.
Her hair was loose around her shoulders, and her face was open.
